sections.heading: How to analyse ANY Union budget — the permanent framework

blocks.text: 'Current budget' questions recur every year with new numbers — so master the **analysis grid**, then plug in the latest February's figures. Grid: (1) **macro stance** — is the fiscal deficit consolidating or expanding, and against what growth assumption? (2) **quality** — capex share and its trend; revenue-deficit direction; (3) **revenue realism** — tax buoyancy assumed vs history, disinvestment credibility; (4) **composition winners** — which sectors gained in real terms (nominal +% minus inflation); (5) **welfare vs investment balance**; (6) **federal impact** — devolution, grants, capex loans to states; (7) **credibility check** — BE vs last year's RE vs Actuals.

sections.heading: Evaluation themes that outlive any single budget

items: **Consolidation with growth**: India cut the deficit ~4.8 points in five years without austerity-style capex cuts — the 'quality consolidation' story; risk: private capex must take the baton as public capex growth plateaus.

**Tax structure**: direct-tax share and the new regime's simplification vs the exemption-ecosystem's end; GST's maturing collections (₹1.8–2 lakh crore monthly runs) but rate-rationalisation pending; the corporate-tax-cut (2019) revenue sacrifice vs investment response debate.

**Welfare architecture**: food subsidy (~₹2 lakh crore) + PM-KISAN + Ujjwala as the floor; critics' point — real-terms stagnation in MGNREGA/education/health vs supporters' point — DBT efficiency and capex's job-creation.
**Credibility**: budget numbers have become MORE honest (off-budget cleanup, realistic nominal-GDP assumptions post-2021) — cite the reversal of the pre-2020 over-projection habit.

**The AP reading of any Union budget**: what did AP gain — devolution share (4.047%), capex-loan allocations, railway/highway outlays in AP, Polavaram provisioning, Amaravati support (the ₹15,000-cr multilateral route featured in July 2024's budget), backward-district funds — a state-lens paragraph earns APPSC marks.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the permanent Union-budget analysis grid

items: **The five lenses to read any budget:** (1) **fiscal stance** (deficit as % of GDP vs the glide path); (2) **quality of spending** (capex-to-revex ratio — capex multiplier ~2.5–3x vs revex ~0.5–1x); (3) **tax buoyancy** (gross tax-to-GDP, direct:indirect mix, share of cesses); (4) **allocative priorities** (capex, welfare, subsidies, defence, interest — the largest single item); (5) **assumptions** (nominal GDP growth, disinvestment, RBI dividend).

**Structural themes that outlive any budget:** the **rising interest burden** (~a quarter of revenue receipts), **subsidy rationalisation** (food, fertiliser, fuel via DBT), **off-budget borrowing transparency**, and the **capex-led vs consumption-led** growth choice.

**Recent direction:** sharply higher **effective capital expenditure**, a new-regime **personal income tax** simplification, PLI-driven manufacturing outlays, and a stated glide toward **fiscal deficit ~4.5% of GDP (2025-26)** with a debt-anchor pivot thereafter.

prelimsPointers: **Capital-expenditure multiplier** (~2.5-3) exceeds the revenue-expenditure multiplier — the case for capex-led budgets.
**Interest payments** are the single largest expenditure item in the Union budget.
FY26 Union budget: fiscal deficit **4.4% of GDP (BE)**; FY25 ~4.8% (RE) — glide path to 'below 4.5% by FY26' achieved.
New income-tax regime (FY26): **nil tax up to ₹12 lakh** via rebate; standard deduction ₹75,000 for salaried.
**PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**: 100 low-productivity agri districts (Aspirational-Districts model for farming).
**Nuclear Energy Mission**: 100 GW by 2047; Small Modular Reactor development; Atomic Energy Act amendments proposed.
50-year **interest-free capex loans to states** ~₹1.5 lakh crore window continues.
From **FY27**, the fiscal rule shifts to a **declining central debt-to-GDP** anchor (toward ~50% by March 2031).
July 2024 budget: **₹15,000 crore Amaravati support** via multilateral agencies — the AP-specific landmark.
mainsAngles: Evaluate the current Union budget on stance, quality and credibility using a structured framework.
Fiscal consolidation without capex compression is India's post-pandemic signature — assess its sustainability as private investment's turn arrives.
Income-tax relief marks a pivot from investment-led to consumption-supported growth — examine the macro logic and risks.
Read the latest Union budget from Andhra Pradesh's seat — devolution, capex loans, Amaravati and Polavaram.
Budgets are credibility documents before they are arithmetic — discuss India's improvement in fiscal transparency.

blocks.text: India's fiscal federalism rests on a **constitutionally mandated umpire** — the **Finance Commission (Art 280**, every five years**)** — correcting the built-in **vertical imbalance** (Centre raises ~60%+ of combined revenue; states incur ~60% of expenditure) and **horizontal imbalance** (income gaps across states). Transfer channels: **tax devolution** (untied — the gold standard), **FC grants** (revenue-deficit, local-body, disaster, sector), **centrally sponsored schemes** (tied, matching), and **capex loans** (the newest window).

rows: Vertical share
**41%** of the divisible pool (1% adjusted for J&K UTs)
**Cesses & surcharges (~15–20% of gross taxes) sit OUTSIDE the pool** — effective state share of gross revenue ~32-33%: the central grievance
Horizontal formula
Income distance 45, population (2011) 15, area 15, forest & ecology 10, **demographic performance 12.5**, tax effort 2.5
2011-census shift penalised early stabilisers — the South's objection; demographic-performance weight was the compensation
Grants
Revenue-deficit grants (AP a major recipient), local bodies (~₹4.36 lakh crore), health, disaster (NDRF/SDRF)
Sector/state-specific grants shrank vs FC-14's design
16th FC
Chair **Arvind Panagariya**; award 2026–31
States' asks: include cesses in the pool, raise share toward 45-50%, weight equity vs efficiency afresh

items: **Design**: constitutional surgery (**101st Amendment, 2016; Arts 246A, 269A, 279A**) pooled sovereignty — one nation, one tax (CGST+SGST/IGST); **GST Council**: Centre 1/3 vote-weight, states 2/3, decisions by 3/4 — Centre holds an effective veto, states collectively hold another.

**Issues ledger**: (a) **compensation cliff** — 14%-growth guarantee ended June 2022; cess extended only to repay COVID loans; (b) **autonomy loss** — states surrendered their most buoyant tax; petroleum/liquor exclusions persist as their residual levers; (c) **rate complexity** — multiple slabs, inverted duties; rationalisation via GoM slow; (d) **IGST settlement & compliance burdens** for small firms; (e) **Mohit Minerals (2022)**: Council recommendations are **not binding** — 'cooperative federalism is a dialogue'; both Parliament and legislatures retain power.

**Scoreboard**: collections matured (₹1.8–2 lakh crore monthly band), e-invoicing curbed evasion, logistics unified (check-posts gone); states' SGST + devolved IGST have grown, but the **perception of centralisation** persists because the guarantee ended just as cesses grew.

**Central assistance beyond FC**: CSS (~₹5 lakh crore universe; 60:40 sharing, 90:10 NE/Himalayan) with matching-burden and one-size critiques (Sub-group of CMs recommended flexi-funds); Special Assistance capex loans; EAP routing; discretionary grants — the **conditionality gradient** from untied devolution to tightly tied schemes is the analytical spine of any federal-finance answer.

sections.heading: The AP brief and answer craft

items: **AP's federal-finance file**: 4.047% inter-se share; large revenue-deficit grants (bifurcation legacy); GST compensation cliff hit a consumption-heavy state; high CSS dependence with matching strain; capex-loan window heavily used; the **16th FC representation** argues bifurcation costs + low per-capita income + demographic performance.

Craft: define the two imbalances → transfer channels by conditionality → 15th FC table → GST five-issue ledger with Mohit Minerals → 16th FC asks → AP paragraph. The **cess-outside-the-pool** point is the single highest-yield criticism; the **dialogue-not-decree** quote is the balancing close.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Federal finance = one diagram (transfer channels by tiedness) + three numbers (41%, 2/3-3/4 Council weights, 60:40 CSS) + two cases (Mohit Minerals; compensation end 2022) + one AP claim. That kit answers GST, FC and central-assistance questions interchangeably.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the transfer architecture & GST bargain

items: **Three channels of transfer:** (1) **Finance Commission** (Art 280) — tax devolution (**41%** divisible pool per the 15th FC) + grants; (2) **centrally sponsored/central-sector schemes**; (3) erstwhile Planning Commission grants, now **NITI Aayog** (advisory, no funds).

**Horizontal-devolution criteria (15th FC):** income distance, population (2011), area, demographic performance, forest & ecology, tax effort — the weightage tussle over the 2011 population is a live federal issue for southern states.

**GST bargain:** states surrendered independent indirect-tax powers for a share of a common tax via the **GST Council (Art 279A)**; the **compensation-cess guarantee** ended in 2022, and *Mohit Minerals (2022)* held Council recommendations are recommendatory — sharpening states' revenue anxiety.
**AP brief:** high dependence on devolution + grants; the SCS/revenue-deficit-grant demands are the concrete stakes; watch the **16th FC (Panagariya, 2026–31)** award.

prelimsPointers: **15th Finance Commission** — vertical devolution **41%**; used **2011 population** with a demographic-performance weight.
**GST Council (Art 279A)** — Union FM (chair) + state FMs; decisions by ≥ ¾ weighted votes.
**Art 280**: FC every five years — taxes distribution, grants principles, local-body augmentation, plus referred matters.
**15th FC devolution: 41%**; horizontal weights — income distance **45%**, population(2011) 15, area 15, forest-ecology 10, demographic performance 12.5, tax effort 2.5.
**Cesses & surcharges lie outside the divisible pool** (Art 270) — the core states' grievance (~15-20% of gross taxes).
**GST Council (Art 279A)**: Centre 1/3, states 2/3 voting weight; decisions need **3/4**; recommendations non-binding (**Mohit Minerals, 2022**).
**GST compensation** (101st Amendment package): 14% growth guarantee for 5 years — ended **June 2022**.
CSS sharing: generally **60:40** (90:10 for NE & Himalayan states) since 2015.
**16th Finance Commission**: chairman **Arvind Panagariya**; award period **2026–31**.
AP's 15th-FC inter-se share: **4.047%**; AP among the largest revenue-deficit-grant states.
mainsAngles: Vertical imbalance is by design; the dispute is over correction — analyse India's transfer architecture by conditionality.
Cesses are unshared taxes by another name — evaluate the erosion of the divisible pool and remedies before the 16th FC.
GST pooled sovereignty without pooling trust — assess the Council's working after the compensation era and Mohit Minerals.
Should Finance Commissions reward performance or need? Examine the 2011-census controversy and the southern states' case.

sections.heading: AP's budget constraints — the post-bifurcation equation

blocks.text: This theme fuses the two threads already built (RMA-012 resources; RMA-013 Act fulfilment) into the **budget-management question**: how does a state that lost its revenue capital, runs persistent revenue deficits and carries ~one-third-of-GSDP debt actually construct its budget — and how does the **central-assistance conflict** shape every line? The constraint set: (1) **committed expenditure** (salaries+pensions+interest ≈ two-thirds of revenue receipts in tight years); (2) **welfare commitments** (DBT calendar politically locked); (3) **FRBM ceilings** now netted for past off-budget borrowing; (4) **contested central flows** (Sec 46 arrears, Polavaram reimbursements, backward-district grants — money budgeted but disputed); (5) GST-compensation cliff since 2022.

items: **What AP books vs what arrives**: successive AP budgets have shown large 'grants-in-aid from Centre' estimates that under-realise — the gap embodies the SCS/Sec-46/Polavaram disputes; analysts read AP budgets by comparing **BE grants vs Actuals** (routinely large shortfalls) — cite this technique.

**Polavaram funding mechanics**: expenditure incurred by the state → reimbursement claims via PPA/CWC scrutiny → delayed/pruned settlements (2013-14 price-level cap dispute; component eligibility) — the cash-flow burden of a 'centrally funded' project falls first on the state.

**The 2024-25 turn**: central budgets explicitly provisioned **Amaravati (₹15,000 cr multilateral route)** and reaffirmed Polavaram support (~₹12,157 cr tranche approved 2024 for phase-1) — conflict shifting to accommodation; an updated answer must carry this arc, not just grievance.

**Evaluation**: AP's budget management is **competent triage under structural deficit** — protecting welfare delivery and debt service while capex leans on Delhi; the risks — arrears culture (pending bills), guarantee build-up, and dependence on politically contingent central goodwill — are the counterweights a balanced answer needs.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — AP's budget constraints, quantified logic

items: **The post-bifurcation equation:** revenue-deficit legacy + loss of Hyderabad's tax base + high committed expenditure (salaries, pensions, interest ≈ a large share of revenue) − thin own-revenue buoyancy = **structural fiscal stress**.
**The welfare-DBT weight:** large direct-benefit and pension outlays lift revenue expenditure and squeeze capex — the 'welfare vs capital investment' trade-off is AP's central budget debate.

**Borrowing & the CAG flags:** heavy reliance on SDL market borrowing and **off-budget borrowing via state corporations/SPVs**, which the CAG has repeatedly flagged as understating the true fiscal deficit.
**Central-assistance conflict:** SCS denial, delayed revenue-deficit grants and Polavaram reimbursements keep AP's budget contingent on Union transfers — the fiscal face of the federalism grievance.

mainsAngles: 'Andhra Pradesh's budget is caught between a welfare imperative and a fiscal constraint' — critically examine.

prelimsPointers: AP's committed expenditure (salaries+pensions+interest) absorbs roughly **two-thirds of revenue receipts** in strained years.
**Sheela Bhide committee** recommends division of Schedule IX/X institution assets between AP and Telangana — largely unresolved.
**Polavaram phase-1**: ~₹12,157 crore central tranche approved (2024) for completion to +41.15m contour.
**Amaravati**: ₹15,000 crore support via World Bank/ADB route announced in the July 2024 Union budget.
AP has repeatedly budgeted central grants that **under-realise against BE** — the fiscal signature of the assistance dispute.
States' ways-and-means advances (WMA) from RBI manage cash mismatches — heavily used by deficit states.
Off-budget borrowings are **netted against borrowing ceilings since 2022** — compressing AP's space.
mainsAngles: Constructing a budget under structural deficit: analyse AP's constraint set and management strategy.
